source.quote: Comp sales were in line with our expectations, decreasing 1.4% compared to a 4.6% increase in the prior year.
If you blend that all together, we probably would have had an annual outlook with a 0 to 2% comp range.
Gross profit increased 5.6% to $165.5 million, and gross margin decreased 60 basis points to 39.2%, in line with our expectations for the quarter.
We expect capital expenditures of $30 million to $35 million, primarily for new stores, IT projects, and store-level initiatives.

We'd anticipate that the third quarter would be above that 40% gross margin target and that the second and fourth quarters, consistent with how it has been in the past because of the Ollie's days and Ollie's Army Night events, would be below that 40% target to come out to the 40 for the year.
The sales exceeded all of our expectations by far, and we talked about it driving 100 points of comp to the quarter.
Gross margin increased 200 basis points to 39.9%, and this was better than our expectations.

With all of this, we feel confident in targeting annual comparable store sales growth of 2% and annual gross margin of 40.5% moving forward acknowledging that there will be some variability to comps and margin between the quarters based on deal flow, seasonality and a few other factors.
Both comparable store sales and earnings were ahead of our expectations and we delivered on all of our strategic objectives in 2025.
